question.question: What caller responsibility preserves snapshot-established membership when an earlier committed configuration entry was already handed out but its ApplyConfChange runs after full snapshot restore?
question.importance: A stale configuration delta could change participant eligibility after recovery. The observed learner-only discrepancy concerns local membership; a voter quorum change, committed conflict or client consequence is not established.
participants: Application owning issued committed-entry work and snapshot installation
Leader producing a later configuration snapshot
contexts: AsyncStorageWrites, reliable FIFO local targets and sequential RawNode calls
Learner add followed by learner removal, fixed three-voter quorum
Full snapshot restore occurs before applying the older add; application still processes the old entry before installing snapshot state
event_paths: ProposeConfChange(add learner) -> actual commitment -> issued apply batch held
Later removal committed/applied on leader -> snapshot/compaction -> automatic MsgSnap -> restore ConfState
Older queued ApplyConfChange -> current configuration delta -> snapshot completion -> Status.Config

supporting_behavior_ids.B_ready_application: Issues committed batches and advances progress independently of snapshot receipt.
supporting_behavior_ids.B_propose_replicate: Produces configuration entries and automatic snapshot delivery.
supporting_behavior_ids.B_aggregate_commit: Establishes the leader prefix underlying the snapshot.
supporting_behavior_ids.B_step_context_and_storage: Snapshot completion advances progress without reinstalling configuration.

counterevidence: Caller may owe a barrier before stepping MsgSnap or suppression of obsolete configuration work; current acquired documentation does not explicitly resolve this.

Synchronous documentation requires Ready updates in order; asynchronous documentation replaces those fields with independent target queues. Their relation to immediate network restore needs a precise applicability interpretation.
The explored add/remove affects only a learner and cannot itself establish a voter-quorum safety violation.
unknowns: Identify whether the selected older ApplyConfChange call is authorized after network full restore, despite originating from an actual issued committed batch.
Compare a caller that completes that older batch before delivering MsgSnap, retaining identical producer inputs, to localize the ordering dependency.
If an applicable preservation responsibility can be sourced, fix it for fresh formal execution rather than relabeling exploratory observations.
question.trigger_rationale: Exploration 71b0b0216b9f493dabbfcc7ac791b691 observed no learner 4 immediately after snapshot restore, learner 4 after the older add, and learner 4 still present after matching snapshot completion at applied/commit 7. The next useful distinction is caller ordering permission and a before-delivery control, not an expanded consensus consequence.

feedback.answered: Exploration 71b0b0216b9f493dabbfcc7ac791b691 completed the actual learner-add/removal and snapshot prefix. Snapshot index 7 excludes learner 4. Public Status.Config excludes 4 after restore, includes 4 after older index-5 ApplyConfChange, and still includes 4 after snapshot completion with applied/commit 7. These are conditional local effects, not formal Evidence or a violation attribution. The shared map records only sourced API and configuration mechanics, not the exploratory result as an implementation invariant.
remaining: Resolve the older call permission and compare before-MsgSnap application as a narrowly informative control.
An independent formal requirement and fresh check are needed before attribution.
